target_customer: OEMs, distributors and VARs selling to US federal and SLED government
problem: Government contractors find it hard to track and win public-sector opportunities; fragmented data (starting with SAM.gov).
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription market network and data (free tier, paid plans); sells to OEMs, resellers, distributors and primes

founders.name: Michael Weiland
previous_startups: Telescope (government contracting opportunities company; outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: CEO. 15 years in government contracting and $2.5B in government sales (YC page). Per TechCrunch (2023-11) he and Nick previously founded Telescope, a government-contracting business; a podcast summary says Govly grew from software built to run that company's internal operations.

founders.name: Nick Weiland
founders.background_notes: Runs engineering and product (YC page). Co-founded Telescope with Mike Weiland (TechCrunch 2023-11).

founders.name: Jon Wright
founders.background_notes: Rose from customer service to VP of Sales in federal IT (YC page).

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating and enriching procurement feeds; standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Network of OEMs and resellers sharing deals could lock in; not evidenced beyond the site.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (2023-11) names Bloomberg and GovWin as competitors. No source shows them copying or buying Govly; Govly instead added free and network features and partnered with distributors (Carahsoft, 2024-10).

market_need_then: Founders came from a government-contracting business where they said compliance and sales needed a whole department (TechCrunch 2023-11). By Nov 2023 Govly reported about 400 organizations (paid and free) and about $1.2M ARR with profitability expected by year-end (company-reported). No 2021 demand data found.

branding.domain_note: Uses govly.com (exact .com); acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical, friendly; positions itself as AngelList for government procurement (Insight Partners)

branding.community_and_virality: Network of 200+ OEMs, VARs and distributors (company-reported); runs Govly Research and a blog; no evidence of fan or press attention to the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear Gov+ly coinage and a clear niche position, with funding and partner press (Insight, Carahsoft), but no evidence of recognition beyond the government-contractor channel; GovLy-like names exist (a 'Govrly' site appears in searches).

outcome_analysis: Govly, YC S21, was built by founders with deep government-contracting experience (previously Telescope) and sold a market network linking OEMs, resellers and distributors. It raised a $9.5M Series A led by Insight Partners in November 2023 at a reported $41M post-money, with about $1.2M ARR and about 400 organizations (company-reported), then added a Carahsoft partnership (October 2024) and AI agents. No exit or shutdown found; total raised reported as $13.1M since 2019, so earlier rounds are missing from the record. Still Active at growth stage, with modest scale so far.
notes: Series A confirmed by Insight Partners' announcement and TechCrunch (both 2023-11-02); the $41M post-money is TechCrunch-reported. Insight says $13.1M raised since 2019, so about $3.6M of earlier funding (including YC) is unlisted; coverage is partial. Competition: GovWin and Bloomberg are named only in 2023 coverage; no source dated near the S21 batch found, so the list is empty. Founding year: YC says 2021, announcements start fundraising in 2019, and Telescope predates Govly. Customer counts differ (about 400 in 2023 per TechCrunch including free users; 200+ per Insight and site). The 2025 Govly 2.0 launch is from a single aggregator. Name origin not found. Headquarters conflicts across profiles (San Francisco, Denver, Washington DC).
